# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 34 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_034_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 5, Chapter 2 — Against Anger

**1** "Put away then from yourself anger and bitterness, and you will be found in your right mind with the Holy Spirit. **2** And take heed to anger, for it is an evil and hurtful spirit. For see how anger destroys the minds of men who have not full faith, how it destroys even the most righteous men. **3** For anger destroys — it is altogether evil; since it is the instrument of the devil. **4** Get yourself free from this anger by exchanging it with long-suffering. For where there is bitterness there is death, and the person who is bitter will not inherit the kingdom of God. **5** Those who are angry, therefore, are overcome by the devil, and are cast away from the Lord, and become corrupted. **6** But those who are patient resist the evil — and when they resist they gain power over him and defeat him. The patient person will live to God, and the long-suffering person will overcome the evil one." **7** I said to him, "Sir, I would like to know the working of anger — how it destroys the minds of the servants of God." **8** He said to me: "Even the most gentle man, when anger comes upon him, becomes exceedingly bitter very quickly — on account of a wife, a child, a servant, a friend, a fellow believer or some other transaction, and he becomes proud and sharp in his talk. **9** After that he becomes completely bitter and remembers neither God nor Christ the Lord, and he speaks words of injustice and lawlessness, adding evil upon evil. **10** So the patience of God is needed; for patience drives away anger and destroys it completely from the heart of the man."

---

*EMET note: Mandate 5.2 — the practical consequences of anger. Anger "destroys the minds" even of the righteous; the antidote is long-suffering/patience. The clinical description of how even a gentle person spirals into bitterness (v.8-9) is psychologically astute.*
